abberufen.why: abberufen is the verb for removing someone from a post or recalling them from a position (einen Botschafter/Geschäftsführer abberufen); candidate_glosses index 1 has it as 'to recall'. The shipped 'withdraw' is the vaguest possible reading of kaikki's first sense and would let a learner reach for abberufen when they mean withdrawing money, troops, or a statement, none of which it covers.

abblasen.why: In ordinary modern German abblasen almost always means to call off an event or plan (das Spiel/den Streik/die Suche abblasen), which candidate_glosses lists at index 2. The shipped literal 'blow off something, blow clear' is a technical sense the learner is unlikely to meet.

abdrehen.why: 'veer' is a narrow nautical/aviation sense. The everyday meaning a learner meets is shutting off a supply at a valve or switch — das Wasser/Gas abdrehen, and in southern German and Austrian usage also lights and appliances — which candidate_glosses gives at index 4. A one-word gloss of 'veer' teaches none of that.

abfeiern.why: The standard sense of abfeiern is taking accrued overtime as time off (Überstunden abfeiern), candidate_glosses index 2. The shipped 'celebrate, praise, love' is the youth-slang reading (das feier ich ab), and as English it is confusing on its own: 'celebrate' reads as plain feiern, which abfeiern does not mean.

abführen.why: The shortening dropped the parenthetical that carried the sense: candidate_glosses index 0 is 'to take away (someone in police custody)'. Bare 'take away' reads as wegnehmen, which abführen never means; the verb is about leading a person away under escort (and separately about remitting taxes or having a laxative effect).

abgleichen.why: 'verify congruence' is not English anyone uses, and it comes from a garbled kaikki entry ('to but check or collate'). abgleichen is comparing two sets of data or accounts to bring them into agreement — reconcile, cross-check, sync (Daten/Termine/Kontostände abgleichen). A learner cannot recover that from the shipped phrase.

abhauen.why: By far the live meaning of abhauen is to clear off or run away (Hau ab!, er ist abgehauen), candidate_glosses index 1. The shipped 'cut off' is the older literal sense of hewing something off with a blade, which survives mainly in fixed phrases and is not what the learner will encounter.

ablenken.why: The everyday sense is distracting someone or their attention (jemanden ablenken, abgelenkt sein), candidate_glosses index 1. Shipped 'divert' alone points at the physics sense of deflecting light or a projectile and invites the wrong use for diverting traffic or a river, which is umleiten.

ablesen.why: The shortening cut kaikki's '(take a reading)' from index 0, leaving a gloss identical to the base verb lesen. ablesen never means reading a book; it is taking a reading off a gauge or meter (den Zählerstand ablesen) or reading aloud from a prepared text.

abrichten.why: The everyday meaning of abrichten is to train an animal (einen Hund abrichten), which candidate_glosses lists as sense 1. The shipped 'drill' is a real but narrow equivalent (drilling troops, or the technical sense of truing a surface, as in Abrichthobel), and as a bare English word it reads first as boring a hole, which is bohren. A learner would take away the wrong verb.

abstechen.old: cut off, cut out, carve out
abstechen.why: Sense 0 describes the spade sense (Torf, Rasenkanten abstechen), which is specialized gardening vocabulary. In ordinary German abstechen means to stab, especially to stab to death (candidate 1, ein Schwein abstechen), or to contrast sharply with something (candidate 3, gegen etwas abstechen). Glossed as 'cut off, cut out, carve out' the verb reads as a synonym of abschneiden, which it is not.

absterben.why: absterben is an ordinary verb meaning that tissue, plants, or limbs die off (abgestorbene Äste; mir ist der Fuß abgestorben), which candidate 2 gives as 'to die back'. 'Atrophy' is both far more technical than the German and semantically off: atrophy is wasting away from disuse, which is verkümmern, whereas absterben is simply dying.

abtreiben.why: The sense a learner meets is the abortion one, candidate 1 (and 2), which is what abtreiben means in essentially all contemporary non-nautical use. The shipped 'go/be sent off course' is the drift sense, restricted to boats and swimmers being carried by wind or current.

abtreten.why: 'Kick away' is a marginal reading. The senses a learner meets are stepping down from an office or a stage (candidates 3 and 4, von einem Amt abtreten) and ceding or handing over rights or territory (Rechte, Gebiete abtreten), the latter missing from candidate_glosses entirely. As shipped the gloss suggests a physical kicking action the verb rarely denotes.

abwägen.why: abwägen is figurative only — to weigh options or arguments against one another (Vor- und Nachteile abwägen). The bare 'weigh' reads as physical weighing and collides directly with abwiegen, which this corpus glosses 'weigh, weigh out'. The parenthetical kaikki carried ('to determine the intrinsic value or merit') was what disambiguated it, and shortening dropped exactly that.

abwählen.why: kaikki's first sense, 'deselect', is the narrow computing/checkbox reading. In ordinary German abwählen means voting an officeholder or government out (eine Regierung abwählen) or dropping a school subject (ein Fach abwählen) — candidate_glosses index 1 carries the political sense. A learner given only 'deselect' will read it as a UI term and miss the two uses actually encountered.

anfallen.why: 'set upon, attack suddenly' is a literary and largely dated sense (von Hunden angefallen werden). The reading a learner meets in modern German is the impersonal one at candidate_glosses index 3 — anfallende Kosten, anfallende Arbeit, wenn Daten anfallen — i.e. costs, work, or data that arise or accrue. Shipping the attack sense teaches a register the learner will not encounter.

angeloben.why: angeloben is chiefly Austrian and its ordinary use is the swearing-in of soldiers, recruits, and officeholders (Angelobung is the standard word for that ceremony) — candidate_glosses index 2, 'to pledge, to swear in'. The shipped 'vow' is the sense of the base verb geloben; a learner who meets angeloben will meet it in the swearing-in reading.

anhaben.old: wear, have on see usage notes
anhaben.why: The trailing 'see usage notes' is Wiktionary editorial scaffolding that survived the shortening of candidate_glosses index 0; it is not part of the meaning and reads as broken English to a learner, who has no usage notes to consult. The meaning itself is correct: to wear, to have on.

anhalten.why: The house style separates synonyms with commas, so 'stop, continue' reads as a pair of equivalents while naming two opposite actions, which is more confusing than helpful. Both are real senses (candidate_glosses indices 0 and 1), but the one a learner meets is 'stop' — er hielt das Auto an, halt an. The 'last, persist' reading is better carried by the participle anhaltend and does not need to share the gloss line.

anhängen.why: The everyday sense of anhängen is physical or digital attachment: einen Anhänger anhängen (hitch a trailer), eine Datei anhängen (attach a file), einen Satz anhängen (append a sentence). The shipped 'weigh on, burden' renders only the figurative dative reading (jemandem etwas anhängen), which is far rarer and is not what a learner meets. The attach sense is absent from candidate_glosses — kaikki's entry here covers only the strong dative verb — so the fix is a rewrite, not an index swap.

anklagen.old: indict by the findings of a jury)
anklagen.why: Mangled shortening of candidate_glosses index 0: the shortening cut out the middle of the parenthetical and left 'indict by the findings of a jury)' with a dangling clause and an unbalanced closing parenthesis. As English it says something false as well — an indictment is not made by a jury's findings in the sense the fragment implies. anklagen means to accuse or, in a legal register, to charge or indict.

anleiten.why: 'guide or to train' is candidate_glosses index 0 pasted with only the first 'to' stripped, leaving a dangling infinitive marker that is ungrammatical in the app's bare-verb-phrase style. The sense is right; anleiten is specifically to instruct or give guidance to someone (Anleitung is a set of instructions).

anreden.why: In English 'begin a talk with someone' reads as starting a lecture or a formal discussion, which anreden does not mean. The verb is to address or speak to someone — it is the verb behind Anrede, the form of address, as in jemanden mit du anreden. The shipped wording is a literal expansion of candidate_glosses index 0 and misses the addressing sense that gives the verb its use.

anvertrauen.why: The shipped gloss is kaikki's sense-group umbrella, not a definition: candidate 0 ends in a colon ('to entrust in various ways:') and the sub-senses that follow are the actual meanings. 'in various ways' describes the dictionary entry's structure, not the verb. The plain meaning is entrust, which candidate_glosses lists at index 1.

aufarbeiten.why: 'Refurbish' is a real but narrow sense (Möbel aufarbeiten). The reading a learner actually meets is working through accumulated material: Rückstände aufarbeiten, die Vergangenheit aufarbeiten, ein Trauma aufarbeiten — the dominant modern usage, and candidate_glosses index 2 ('to mentally process; to bring clarity to'). The importer took kaikki's first-listed sense over the common one.

aufatmen.why: kaikki's sole gloss is a literal reading of auf + atmen. The verb means to breathe out in relief — erleichtert aufatmen — and the relief component is the meaning, not an overtone. 'Breathe again' invites the learner to use it for resuming breathing, which is wieder atmen.

aufbleiben.why: The leading 'wake' is kaikki's archaic intransitive English (as in keeping a vigil), not the modern reading. In the salient first position it maps aufbleiben onto aufwachen/aufwecken, which it never means. The trailing synonyms carry the actual sense; the first item should simply go.

auferwecken.why: auferwecken is the elevated, religious causative of auferstehen: to raise someone from the dead (Lazarus auferwecken). 'Raise up, awaken' is vague enough to read as ordinary waking, which collides with aufwecken — a near-homograph the learner will also meet. The app already glosses auferstehen 'be resurrected, rise from the dead'; the transitive partner should mirror it.

auflegen.why: The shipped 'lay on' is kaikki's first-listed literal sense, but the reading a learner actually meets is telephonic: 'Ich lege jetzt auf' (I'm hanging up now) is the everyday use, and candidate_glosses lists 'to hang up' at index 1. The DJ sense (Platten auflegen, index 4) is also more current than bare 'lay on'.

auflehnen.why: In actual use auflehnen is essentially always reflexive and means to rebel or revolt: 'sich gegen die Obrigkeit auflehnen'. The physical 'lean one's arms on' reading behind the shipped 'lean on' is marginal and, as a bare gloss, collides with anlehnen and sich stützen auf. candidate_glosses has the right sense at index 1.

aufschieben.why: The dominant sense is temporal — to postpone or defer, as in 'die Entscheidung aufschieben' (hence Aufschieberitis for procrastination). The shipped 'push open' is the literal spatial reading, restricted to things that slide (a bolt, a sliding door), and is much rarer. candidate_glosses lists 'to postpone' at index 1.

aufschlagen.why: 'pitch, serve' ships kaikki's first sense, a narrow sports reading, and in English the pair is doubly opaque because 'pitch' reads as baseball rather than as the tennis serve intended. The senses a learner meets are 'ein Buch aufschlagen' (open a book — candidate index 3) and 'auf dem Boden aufschlagen' (hit, impact — index 5).

aufsetzen.why: The shortening dropped the part that carried the meaning: candidate index 0 is 'to put on (something to be worn on the head)'. Bare 'put on' invites the learner to use aufsetzen for clothing generally, which takes anziehen — one aufsetzt a Hut, Mütze, or Brille, not Schuhe.

aufsteigen.why: Mounting a horse or bicycle is a specialized application of aufsteigen, and it is first in kaikki only by entry order. The central sense is upward motion — Rauch/Nebel steigt auf, ein Ballon steigt auf — with the promotion senses (beruflich aufsteigen, in die Bundesliga aufsteigen) following from it. That is candidate_glosses index 2 ("to rise, to ascend"). "get on, mount" leaves the learner unable to read the ordinary uses.

aufstören.why: "pattern up" is not English and names no action; it is a corrupt Wiktionary entry that the importer took verbatim as the sole candidate (index 0). German aufstören means to rouse or startle something out of rest — aufscheuchen — as in Wild aufstören, and figuratively to stir up or unsettle. A learner cannot recover any meaning from the shipped gloss.

auftreiben.why: "bloat" is a real but marginal sense (a distended belly, dough rising). The dominant modern use is procuring something with difficulty — Wo soll ich so schnell Geld auftreiben?, einen Ersatzteil auftreiben — which is candidate_glosses index 3 ("to find, to get, to get hold of, to come by"). The importer took kaikki's first-listed sense and shipped the rare one.

aufwarten.why: "serve, wait" is the dated servant sense (jemandem bei Tisch aufwarten), marked veraltet in contemporary usage. The current everyday construction is mit etwas aufwarten — mit einer Überraschung, mit Zahlen aufwarten — which is candidate_glosses index 2 ("to offer, to serve up"). The English is also actively confusing: bare "wait" reads as warten (wait for), which is the wrong verb entirely.

aufzeichnen.why: "plot, chart" is the narrow technical sense (a curve on graph paper) and is what kaikki happens to list first. The sense a learner meets is recording — eine Sendung aufzeichnen, ein Gespräch aufzeichnen — which is candidate_glosses index 2 ("to record, to note"), plus the plain drawing sense. Shipping the graph-paper reading leaves the learner without the everyday word.

ausbleiben.why: "be absent" invites the learner to use ausbleiben of a person missing from school or work, which takes fehlen. Ausbleiben is said of an expected event or result that never arrives — der Erfolg blieb aus, die Reaktion blieb nicht aus. The gloss is broadly in the right area but points at the wrong subject.

ausbringen.why: The shortening cut away the part that carried the meaning. candidate_glosses index 0 reads "to raise, to utter (something) in front of others which they echo or react to" — that is the toast sense, einen Trinkspruch auf jemanden ausbringen. Reduced to bare "raise", the gloss reads as heben or erhöhen, which ausbringen does not mean; the other live sense is agricultural spreading (Gülle ausbringen).

ausholen.why: As a bare two-word gloss, 'haul off' does not convey the verb. In ordinary English 'haul off' reads as carrying something away, and the striking sense survives only in the fixed American idiom 'haul off and hit someone'. The kaikki parenthetical that carried the actual meaning ('to draw back the arm in order to punch') was dropped in shortening. German ausholen is winding the arm back before a blow, and by extension (weit ausholen) starting a story far back.

auslernen.why: 'finish learning' is a literal calque that fits the proverb 'man lernt nie aus' but not the verb's ordinary use, which is specifically completing a vocational apprenticeship: 'sie hat ausgelernt' means she is now fully trained. A learner given 'finish learning' would build ungrammatical sentences like 'ich habe das Buch ausgelernt'. kaikki offers nothing better, so this is a judgment call rather than an import defect.

auslesen.why: 'cull' is the etymologically faithful rendering of the pick-out sense, but in modern English the word is dominated by the selective-slaughter sense, which German auslesen never carries. The readings a learner actually meets are 'select, pick out' (candidate_glosses index 2, cf. Auslese for selected grapes) and 'read out' of data (index 1). A one-word gloss of 'cull' teaches the wrong action.

ausscheiden.why: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first-listed physiological sense, which is both technical and imprecise: German ausscheiden is excretion (elimination), not secretion, which is absondern or sezernieren. The sense a learner meets is dropping out of a competition or leaving a post — 'Deutschland ist im Viertelfinale ausgeschieden' — which candidate_glosses lists at index 2.

ausscheren.why: 'sheer, sheer out' is nautical jargon opaque to a learner, and the verb 'sheer' collides with the far more familiar adjective (sheer drop, sheer nonsense). The everyday sense is a vehicle pulling out of line or changing lanes, and figuratively breaking ranks with a group; candidate_glosses lists this at index 1.

ausschreiben.why: English 'advertise' defaults to promoting a product or service, which ausschreiben never means; that is werben fuer. The verb covers putting a position or contract out for open application or tender (eine Stelle ausschreiben) and, separately, writing something out in full (eine Zahl ausschreiben). candidate_glosses indices 1, 3 and 5 all point at the tender sense, so index 0's unqualified 'advertise' is a shortening that lost the qualifier.

austrinken.why: The verb means to drink something to the last drop (Duden: ganz leer trinken); the emptying is only the result and the drinking is the criterial part. The shipped 'empty' comes from candidate_glosses index 0, kaikki's bare 'to empty', which strips exactly the component that distinguishes austrinken from leeren. As shipped, a learner would use austrinken for emptying a box or a room. Index 2, 'to finish one's drink', is the sense actually meant.

ausziehen.why: Both shipped senses are real, but kaikki's entry order is not frequency order here: Duden leads with the clothing sense, and 'take off / undress' is what a learner meets first and hears most (zieh die Schuhe aus, sich ausziehen). candidate_glosses indices 2 through 4 all cover it. Shipping only 'move out, vacate' leaves the everyday sense unrepresented.

bedingen.old: have agreed upon as a contractual term
bedingen.why: The shipped gloss is kaikki's sense 0, the archaic legal/contractual reading that survives today mainly in the reflexive sich etwas ausbedingen and in the obsolete strong forms bedang/bedungen. Living modern bedingen is causal: 'Das bedingt hohe Kosten', 'bedingt durch das Wetter'. That meaning is already in candidate_glosses at index 1 ('to require, have as a prerequisite or condition') and index 2 ('to cause'), so this is a mechanical first-sense import defect. The shipped phrase is also unusable as a short gloss: a learner cannot recover the verb's everyday meaning from it.

befallen.why: 'affect' is too weak and collides with beeinflussen and beeinträchtigen — beeinträchtigen ships as 'impair, affect' in this same shard. befallen is the verb of disease, pests, and sudden emotion seizing a subject: 'von Schädlingen befallen', 'Angst befiel ihn'. The precise senses are in candidate_glosses at index 1 ('to seize') and index 2 ('to infest'). A learner given 'affect' would produce neutral-causation sentences the verb cannot carry.

befühlen.why: 'palpate' is medical jargon opaque to most English speakers, and the German verb it actually translates is abtasten (or palpieren). befühlen is everyday German for running one's hands over something to feel it — 'den Stoff befühlen'. kaikki offers only this one candidate, so the register mismatch came in unfiltered rather than from a wrong-sense pick.

beikommen.why: 'come here' is kaikki's sense 0 but corresponds to Duden's landschaftlich (regional) reading 'herankommen'. Standard beikommen takes the dative and means to get at, cope with, or tackle someone or something: 'dem Problem ist nicht beizukommen', 'ihm ist schwer beizukommen'. That is candidate_glosses index 1 ('to deal with'), so the common sense was available and passed over.

beklagen.why: The lead synonym 'pity' points at bemitleiden, which ships in this same corpus glossed exactly 'pity'. beklagen is to lament, bemoan, or deplore — Verluste beklagen, die zu beklagenden Opfer — with reflexive sich beklagen meaning complain. 'Lament' is present in candidate 0 but arrives second, behind the reading that collides.

belachen.why: 'Belaugh' is not usable English — it is a Wiktionary calque of the German prefixation, not a word a learner will ever encounter or be understood using. The first synonym carries the meaning correctly, so the gloss is not unusable, but the second half is noise imported verbatim from candidate 0.

bemeistern.why: bemeistern means to get something under control — to master or overcome it (seine Angst bemeistern, die Lage bemeistern). 'Dominate' names a different action, the one carried by beherrschen or dominieren, and a learner taught it would use bemeistern for holding power over people rather than for overcoming a difficulty. The correct sense is not in candidate_glosses; kaikki's single entry is itself the weak rendering.

bepflanzen.why: bepflanzen takes the ground as its object, not the plant: ein Beet bepflanzen is to plant a bed with something, while planting a tree is pflanzen or einpflanzen. The bare gloss 'plant' loses the be- prefix's applicative force and invites the error einen Baum bepflanzen. candidate 0 preserves the distinction with its '(supply with plants)' rider, which the shortening dropped.

berücken.why: The literal 'ensnare' (catching game in a Rücke, a snare) is the obsolete hunting sense. In all living use berücken means to enchant or charm — Duden glosses it 'in seinen Bann ziehen, bezaubern', and the participle berückend ('berückend schön') is how a learner actually meets the word. candidate_glosses index 1, 'to captivate', is the sense that should have shipped; English 'ensnare' additionally carries a connotation of trickery that the German does not.

bescheiden.old: confer the decision or fate formally
bescheiden.why: 'Confer the decision or fate formally' is not English one can use — you do not confer a decision on someone — and it leaves the learner without a usable verb. The transitive verb is Amtsdeutsch: jemanden abschlägig bescheiden = to give someone a formal (negative) ruling, i.e. to notify them of an official decision. candidate_glosses index 0 also offers 'to announce, to proclaim', which is closer to usable but too broad; the notification-of-a-decision element is the whole point of the word.

beschenken.why: 'Endow' in English means to fund an institution or to be furnished with a quality, neither of which beschenken does. jemanden beschenken is the everyday word for giving somebody presents — what happens at Weihnachten and Geburtstage. candidate_glosses index 1, 'to present, to gift', is the sense a learner meets.

beschicken.why: 'Send' is right for eine Messe/Konferenz beschicken (to send exhibits or delegates to), but 'commit' is not English one can use for this verb — it pulls toward committing a crime or committing resources. It also omits the verb's most frequent modern use, the technical one: einen Ofen, Reaktor or eine Maschine beschicken = to charge or feed it, which candidate_glosses index 1 covers with 'to load'.

beschneiden.why: Circumcision is a real sense but a specialized one. The senses a learner actually meets are horticultural (Hecken, Bäume, Sträucher beschneiden) and figurative (Rechte, Freiheiten, Befugnisse beschneiden) — the latter is among the verb's most frequent collocations in journalistic German, and Duden lists the trimming sense first. candidate_glosses index 1, 'to trim; to prune', should have shipped, extended with the curtail reading.

bespringen.why: The gloss is a Wiktionary cross-reference, not a meaning: 'synonym of begatten' tells an English-speaking learner nothing, and the target verb is itself untranslated. bespringen is the animal-husbandry word for a male mounting a female to breed — the ':' clause kaikki appended, 'to cover', is the English term of art but is opaque standing alone.

bestecken.why: 'Get stuck' is the rare intransitive reading (a vessel or plough besteckt = comes to a standstill), archaic outside nautical and agricultural usage. The living verb is transitive and means to set things into a surface: einen Kranz mit Blumen bestecken, einen Braten mit Speck bestecken. candidate_glosses index 1 has it. As shipped, the gloss names an action with the opposite valency from what the verb does.

bestärken.why: bestärken takes a person as its object and means to reinforce or confirm someone in a belief, resolve, or opinion (jemanden in seiner Meinung bestärken). Leading with 'strengthen' and closing with 'fortify' points the learner at physical strengthening, which is stärken/verstärken, not bestärken; a learner reading this gloss would plausibly write 'die Mauer bestärken'. candidate_glosses index 1 ('to confirm, to reinforce') carries the actual sense.

beweinen.why: The meaning is right, but this is kaikki's unfiltered synonym list rather than a gloss. 'beweep' is not modern English — it survives only in Shakespeare — and contributes nothing a learner can use, while four comma-separated synonyms overrun the house style. 'mourn, cry over' names the sense completely.

dahinsterben.why: "die" is the gloss for plain sterben and drops everything the dahin- prefix contributes. Like dahinsiechen and dahinvegetieren, this verb names a gradual dying — wasting away over time, or a population dying off one after another — not the event of death.

daransetzen.why: Shortening destroyed the sense. kaikki's sense 0 is "to risk, to not spare, to make (every effort), to use"; stripping the parenthetical left "make" and "use" as bare verbs, and "not spare" as a fragment. The result reads as four unrelated generic verbs rather than a meaning. The verb lives almost entirely in the collocation "alles daransetzen" / "seine ganze Kraft daransetzen": to stake something on an aim, to devote all one's effort to it.

darniederliegen.why: "be sick" is faithful to candidate_glosses index 0 but misleads twice: in British English "be sick" reads as "vomit", and the elevated German verb applies well beyond illness — die Wirtschaft / der Handel liegt darnieder. The sense is lying prostrate, laid low, in a slump; index 1 ("to languish") is closer.

davontragen.why: The literal sense was shipped over the ones the verb actually carries in use. Plain "carry away" is expressed by wegtragen; davontragen is nearly always figurative — Verletzungen/einen Schaden davontragen (sustain an injury), den Sieg/den Preis davontragen (carry off the victory). Those are candidate_glosses indices 1 ("to achieve, obtain") and 2 ("to suffer").

dazukommen.why: "arrive" collides with ankommen and does not name what dazukommen does. The verb means to join something already in progress or, very commonly, to be added on top of what precedes — "dazu kommt, dass …" (on top of that …). candidate_glosses index 1 is "to be added"; the joining sense is what a learner meets first.

draufgeben.why: Ungrammatical English produced by dropping a parenthetical. kaikki sense 0 is "to add (on top) of something"; deleting "(on top)" leaves "add of something", which is not a usable phrase. The verb means to add something on top of what is already there (etwas draufgeben).

durchbringen.why: The shipped gloss is candidate 0 with its scaffolding intact: 'be able to' is modal framing from the dictionary wording, not part of the verb's meaning, so the phrase names no action a learner can attach to durchbringen. The senses actually met are 'get someone through' (an illness, an exam, a bill) and 'support, keep fed' — candidates 2 through 5 all cluster there.

durchfallen.why: The importer took the compositional literal sense. In use durchfallen almost always means to fail an exam or test (durch die Prüfung durchfallen), which candidate_glosses lists as sense 1 ('to fail, to not pass'). A learner shown 'fall through' will not recognize the verb in the context where it actually appears.

durchschauen.why: Candidate 0 reads 'to see through (e.g. a window, telescope)'; the shortening dropped the parenthetical that was doing the disambiguating work. Bare English 'see through' overwhelmingly means detecting a deception, which is the meaning of the inseparable durchscháuen (jemanden durchschauen), not of the literal separable verb glossed here. 'look through' names the intended sense unambiguously, and matches how durchblicken is glossed in this same corpus.

durchziehen.why: 'pass' is candidate 0 taken verbatim, and on its own it is too vague to identify the verb — it reads as passing an exam or handing something over, neither of which durchziehen means. The senses a learner meets are the literal 'pull through' (candidate 3) and the very common colloquial 'etwas durchziehen', to go through with something and see it to the end.

einbilden.why: The shortening dropped the '(falsely)' in candidate 0, and that word carried the whole distinction. Reflexive sich etwas einbilden means to imagine something that is not so, to fancy or delude oneself; plain 'imagine' collides with sich vorstellen, which is the neutral verb and the one a learner will otherwise reach for.

einkehren.why: "sojourn" is archaic English and loses what the verb actually names: stopping off at an inn or restaurant during a walk or journey ("wir sind im Gasthaus eingekehrt"). A learner reading "sojourn" would take it for a general word for staying somewhere, which is einkehren's figurative extension at best ("Ruhe kehrte ein"). Neither candidate gloss is usable; the correct sense is absent from the list.

einkommen.why: "earn" is the action of verdienen and would license the wrong German: einkommen is not a transitive verb of earning, and *"Ich komme 3000 Euro ein" is not German. The verb is intransitive and formal — money, donations, or entries come in ("die eingekommenen Spenden"), or one petitions for something ("um etwas einkommen"). The money-arriving sense is not in candidate_glosses; index 1 is the unrelated sports sense of placing in a ranking.

einreisen.why: "travel" belongs to reisen, not einreisen, and bare "enter" collides with betreten/eintreten for entering a room. einreisen means specifically to cross a border into a country ("nach Deutschland einreisen"); the country is not an optional nuance but the whole content of the ein-. The single candidate gloss carries the same defect, so the fix is not an index swap.

einschneiden.why: "engrave" points at gravieren and away from the core sense, which is simply cutting into a surface or making an incision ("eine Kerbe einschneiden"), plus the everyday physical sense of a strap or waistband digging in ("der Riemen schneidet ein"). "carve" is defensible for "seinen Namen in die Rinde einschneiden" and worth keeping alongside, but leading with the engraving reading misdirects.

einschreiben.why: The literal "write into, inscribe" is kaikki's first-listed sense but the reading a learner meets is reflexive: sich einschreiben = to enroll or register, above all at a university. That sense is candidate_glosses index 2 ("to enroll, enlist"). The registered-mail sense at index 1 is the other one in daily use; the inscribing sense is the rarest of the three.

einschulen.old: instruct for a specific position, task
einschulen.why: The shipped gloss is the Austrian workplace sense (einschulen = einarbeiten, train someone for a job), which in Germany is rare. The standard meaning is enrolling a child in school — "das Kind wird im September eingeschult" — which is candidate_glosses index 1 ("to accept a pupil into the first grade"). The shipped phrasing is also a dictionary paraphrase rather than a gloss.

einstellen.why: 'set, hire' joins two unrelated senses with a comma, which house style reads as 'these mean the same thing'. Both are real senses of einstellen (candidate indices 1 and 0), but presented as synonyms they teach neither. The sense to commit to is adjusting or setting something — the one behind the everyday noun Einstellungen ('settings') and behind sich einstellen auf.

eintreiben.why: The importer took kaikki sense 0, the literal 'drive in' (cattle, a nail). The sense a learner actually meets is the one at candidate index 1: collecting money that is owed — Schulden eintreiben, Steuern eintreiben, Außenstände eintreiben. 'drive in' also collides with einschlagen/einfahren in a learner's mind.

einwenden.why: The shortening kept only the bare verbs from kaikki sense 0 ('to raise (an objection to), to make (an argument against)') and dropped the parenthesized objects that carried the entire meaning. 'raise, make' names no action a learner can attach to einwenden; the verb means to object or to raise an objection ('dagegen ist nichts einzuwenden').

einüben.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus: the gloss carries a stray '#' sense separator and the unstripped infinitival 'to practice / practise' from kaikki sense 0. As shipped it is not English about the verb. einüben means to practice or rehearse something until it is mastered (ein Stück, einen Ablauf einüben).

entbinden.old: see a woman through childbirth, deliver
entbinden.why: The shipped gloss is kaikki sense 0 written from the attendant's perspective ('see a woman through childbirth'), which is the obstetric usage. The reading a learner meets is intransitive and takes the mother as subject — 'Sie hat gestern entbunden' — which candidate index 1 and 2 both give as 'to give birth'. The current wording also pairs that clinical sense with 'deliver' across a comma, presenting two different perspectives as synonyms.

entfahren.why: Bare 'escape' points a learner at entfliehen/entkommen — escaping a place or captor — which entfahren does not mean. Its living use is the involuntary utterance: a word, cry, or curse escapes someone's lips ('ein Fluch entfuhr ihm'), which candidate index 1 gives as 'to slip out (someone's) mouth'. The subject is the utterance, not the person.

entheben.why: 'relieve' standing alone reads in English as relieve pain or relieve pressure, which is erleichtern or lindern, not entheben. Entheben takes a genitive of the thing someone is freed from and its live use is jemanden seines Amtes entheben — remove from office, relieve of duty (hence Amtsenthebung). The gloss points at the right action but the one word most learners will resolve it to is the wrong verb.

entrücken.why: Both words in the shipped gloss name the wrong action to any learner. 'translate' is the archaic theological sense (as in 'Enoch was translated to heaven'), and a German learner will read it as übersetzen — the single most confusable false lead possible in a language app. 'rapture' as a transitive verb is not ordinary English either. The verb means to carry someone off to another place or state, and in living use it is the mental/spiritual sense: die Musik entrückte ihn, and the participle entrückt 'rapt, in a trance, far away'. candidate_glosses has this at index 1 ('to ravish, to enrapture, to enthrall (spiritually)') and index 2 ('to transport, to carry away (mentally)'); the importer took index 0.

entschlafen.why: Correct as far as it goes, but leading with 'fall asleep' invites the error the verb is most likely to cause: a learner glossing entschlafen onto einschlafen and writing ich bin gestern früh entschlafen. Modern entschlafen is a euphemism for dying (sanft entschlafen, die Entschlafenen) and is not used for ordinary sleep. Putting 'die' second, after a comma the house style reads as 'these mean the same thing', understates that the death sense is the only one in use.

ergehen.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus. 'forms the perfect with sein' is Wiktionary's auxiliary-selection header for the sense group that follows (candidate_glosses index 0), not a meaning; the importer took it as sense 0. It tells the learner nothing about the verb. The sense a learner actually meets is the impersonal one in 'Wie ist es dir ergangen?' / 'Es erging ihm schlecht' — how someone fared, which is candidate_glosses index 2. The legal 'be issued' sense (index 1, 'ein Urteil ergeht') is the other real reading but is confined to officialese.

erhoffen.why: kaikki's 'to hope (for); desire; want (to)' used semicolons to separate loose paraphrases; flattening them to commas presents 'desire' and 'want' as synonyms of the verb. Erhoffen (nearly always reflexive: 'sich etwas von etwas erhoffen') means specifically to hope for or hope to gain something, and glossing it as 'want' invites a learner to substitute it for wollen or wünschen, which it cannot do.

erlöschen.why: The shipped gloss makes this a transitive verb of putting fires out, which is löschen (or auslöschen). The strong verb erlöschen (erlischt, erlosch, ist erloschen) is intransitive: a flame or light goes out on its own (die Kerze erlosch), and by extension a right, warranty, contract, or family line lapses or dies out (der Anspruch erlischt). candidate_glosses offers only the transitive reading, so the correct sense is not in the list — this is a wrong-entry import rather than a wrong-index one. A learner taught 'extinguish' will write ich erlösche das Feuer, which is not German.

erraten.why: 'determine through advice or empathy' is an archaic sense preserved from the older meaning of raten (advise), and as English it barely reads as a verb meaning at all. The verb a learner meets is 'guess correctly' — Rate mal! … Du hast es erraten! — which is candidate_glosses index 1, 'to guess (something) correctly, to divine'. The importer took kaikki's first-listed sense over the only living one.

ersehen.why: kaikki's bare 'to learn' loses what distinguishes this verb: ersehen is nearly always aus etwas ersehen, to gather or discern something from a document or set of facts (wie aus dem Bericht zu ersehen ist). As shipped it collides head-on with lernen and with erlernen, which this same corpus glosses 'learn, acquire', so the learner has no way to tell the three apart.

erstatten.why: The comma presents 'reimburse' and 'file' as synonyms, but they are two unrelated senses, and 'file' is uninterpretable on its own: it is a fragment of the fixed collocation Anzeige erstatten (file a complaint) / Bericht erstatten (make a report), where the meaning lives in the noun. Keeping 'reimburse' — the sense that works with a free object, as in Kosten erstatten — and dropping the stranded fragment.

ersterben.why: Plain 'die' of a person or animal is sterben; ersterben is not used that way in modern German. It survives almost exclusively in the figurative sense of a sound, motion, or expression fading out — der Lärm erstarb, das Lächeln erstarb auf ihren Lippen. That is candidate_glosses index 1, 'to die away, to gradually stop'. The shipped gloss both duplicates sterben and sends the learner to the wrong register.

erwachsen.why: 'grow up' is what aufwachsen means, and it is almost certainly first in kaikki because the participle erwachsen became the adjective for 'adult'. As a finite verb in modern German, erwachsen means to arise or spring from something: daraus erwuchsen erhebliche Probleme, ihm erwuchs daraus ein Vorteil. That is candidate_glosses index 1 ('to spring up, to spring from, to proceed from') and index 4 ('to arise (difficulties, tasks)'). A learner given 'grow up' will reach for erwachsen where only aufwachsen works.

erweichen.why: erweichen means to make or become soft — Wachs erweichen — and figuratively to soften someone's resolve or move them. It does not mean 'weaken' in the sense of reducing strength; that is schwächen. Leading the gloss with 'weaken' (kaikki's own wording at index 0) invites a learner to reach for erweichen where schwächen is required. 'soften' alone carries both the literal and the figurative reading.

erziehen.why: erziehen is the ordinary German verb for bringing a child up — Kinder erziehen, gut erzogen, Erziehung 'upbringing'. It names the formative, disciplinary business of raising someone, not the fostering-and-caring sense that English 'nurture' denotes (that is pflegen or hegen). kaikki's 'to nurture' is its first-listed sense and was taken verbatim; sense 1, 'to educate', is closer, but the gloss a learner needs is 'raise, bring up'.

festfrieren.why: festfrieren means to freeze fast to something so that it can no longer be moved — das Boot ist am Ufer festgefroren. The shipped 'ice over, freeze' describes a surface becoming covered in ice, which is zufrieren or vereisen, and drops the fest- component that is the whole point of the compound. Same shape as the zuschwellen 'swell up' case.

festhalten.why: Both halves name real senses, but the comma makes them read as synonyms, so the learner is told that 'hold on' and 'record' are the same action. They are candidate senses 0/1 and 5 respectively — grip-and-not-let-go versus documenting an event in writing or on film. The sense a learner meets first and most often is the physical one, so the gloss should commit to it.

feststehen.why: English 'stand firm' names refusing to yield under pressure, which is standhalten or festbleiben, not feststehen. German feststehen is predicated of facts and arrangements: 'Es steht fest, dass…', 'Der Termin steht fest' — to be settled, established, beyond doubt. kaikki offers only the literal fest+stehen reading, so no correct sense is in candidate_glosses; the shipped gloss teaches a learner to use the verb of certainty for acts of resolve.

fortfahren.why: The sense a learner meets is 'continue, carry on' — 'Fahren Sie bitte fort', 'mit der Arbeit fortfahren' — which candidate_glosses lists at index 2 and 3. The shipped 'drive away, drive off' is the literal vehicular reading, which is possible but marginal in modern usage and is normally covered by wegfahren or losfahren.

fortgehen.old: continue, go on, keep on, carry on
fortgehen.why: The primary sense is departure — 'Er ist fortgegangen' — a straight synonym of weggehen, which candidate_glosses lists at index 1. The shipped 'continue, go on, keep on, carry on' is the impersonal reading used of processes ('die Arbeit geht fort'), which is both rarer and better served by fortdauern or weitergehen. Four synonyms for the secondary sense also crowds out the one a learner needs.

fortschleifen.old: synonym of wegschleifen: to drag away
fortschleifen.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus: the gloss is a cross-reference to another German verb rather than English about this one, and it names wegschleifen — a word the learner has no reason to know — before delivering any meaning. Only the tail 'drag away' is a gloss.

freimachen.why: 'Put a stamp on' is the postal-clerk sense (frankieren), a technical usage a learner will essentially never meet, especially now that franking is machine-done. The senses in live use are clearing or freeing something up — 'die Straße freimachen', 'sich einen Nachmittag freimachen' — candidate_glosses index 1, plus the reflexive 'undress' heard at a doctor's office.

freuen.why: The comma pairs the reflexive sense with the transitive one as if they were synonyms, so the learner is shown 'be happy' and 'please' as equivalents when they are converse valencies (sich freuen versus es freut mich). Worse, 'be happy, please' parses on sight as an imperative with the politeness word attached. The sense a learner meets first is the reflexive one, candidate_glosses index 1.

fällen.why: The bare 'pass' carries no meaning without its object: it is intelligible only if the learner already knows 'ein Urteil fällen'. As shipped it reads as a second synonym of 'fell', which it is not. The core sense is felling a tree, candidate_glosses index 0.

geraten.why: The comma joins two genuinely different senses, which the house style reads as synonymy: 'get into' is candidate sense 3 (in Panik/Schwierigkeiten/Vergessenheit geraten) and 'turn out' is candidate sense 0 (der Kuchen ist gut geraten). The dominant sense a learner meets by far is the first, unintentional-arrival one, so the gloss should commit to it with true synonyms rather than pair it with an unrelated reading.

gewarten.why: The shortening preserved kaikki's internal alternation 'to await or wait for' verbatim, so the shipped gloss carries a dictionary 'or' that no other gloss in the corpus uses. The sense is right; only the phrasing is lifted apparatus. House style would list the synonyms with commas.

haushalten.why: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first sense, the literal 'run a household', which is the dated reading; modern usage is overwhelmingly 'mit etwas haushalten' — to use a resource sparingly (mit den Kräften/Ressourcen/dem Geld haushalten). DWDS and Duden both give the economizing sense as the live one, and it is candidate_glosses index 1. A learner meeting haushalten in text will almost always meet it with 'mit' plus a resource, not as a synonym for einen Haushalt führen.

herausbrechen.why: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first sense, the narrow figurative one that only works in the frame 'es brach aus ihm heraus' (words bursting out of someone). The sense a learner meets is the literal one at candidate_glosses index 1: forcibly breaking a piece out of something, or a piece breaking off (einen Zahn herausbrechen, ein Stück aus der Mauer herausbrechen). Standing alone as English, 'burst out' also reads as burst out laughing or burst out of a room, neither of which this verb means.

herausgeben.why: 'publish' is right, but 'hand out' names the wrong action for the second sense. herausgeben is handing something over or giving it back to its owner — surrendering documents, giving change (Geld herausgeben) — not distributing copies to a group, which is verteilen or austeilen. A learner taking 'hand out' at face value would produce 'Flyer herausgeben', which German does not say. candidate_glosses index 1 has it as 'to hand over, to give, to restitute'; the safe fix is to keep the publishing sense the gloss already leads with and drop the misleading second term.

heraushalten.new: keep out of, stay out of
heraushalten.why: The shipped gloss is the literal physical sense (holding something out a window), which is real but marginal. In use the verb is overwhelmingly reflexive: 'sich aus etwas heraushalten', 'halt dich da raus' — candidate index 2, 'to keep oneself away from something'. That is the sense a learner will meet.

herausschreiben.why: English 'write out' reads as writing something in full or in longhand. The German means extracting by writing — copying quotations, figures, or vocabulary out of a source, which is what kaikki's '(i.e. of a work)' was pointing at.

herausstellen.why: The comma presents two unrelated senses as synonyms: 'turn out' is reflexive 'sich herausstellen' (candidate index 4) while 'highlight' is transitive emphasis (candidate index 1). The sense a learner meets constantly is the reflexive one, in 'es stellte sich heraus, dass ...'. Ship that alone rather than pairing it with a different sense.

herausziehen.why: Shortening candidate index 0 'to pull (out)' dropped the parenthesized 'out', so the gloss collapses onto simplex 'ziehen'. The heraus- prefix is the whole content of the verb: extraction, as in a splinter, a plug, or a tooth.

hermachen.why: The gloss is ungrammatical English ('a impression') and was cut from kaikki's sense 0 'to make a (specified) impression', losing the parenthetical that carried the meaning: the verb needs a quantifier ('viel/wenig hermachen' = look impressive / not look like much) and does not mean 'make an impression' in the English idiomatic sense of impressing a person. Sense 1 ('sich über etwas hermachen' = get busy with, tackle) is the other reading a learner meets.

herumkommen.why: 'move round something' is kaikki's literal first sense and is the least-used reading. The everyday idiom is 'um etwas nicht herumkommen' — candidate index 2, being unable to avoid something ('da kommst du nicht drum herum'); the other live sense is candidate index 1, 'viel herumkommen' = travel widely. Either would serve a learner better than the literal one.

hervorsehen.why: The shortening dropped kaikki's '(of an object)' and left a bare transitive-looking 'show'. Hervorsehen is intransitive: something protrudes into view from behind or beneath something else — 'das Taschentuch sah aus der Jackentasche hervor'. Glossed as 'show', a learner would take it for a synonym of zeigen.

hinauslaufen.why: In modern German this verb is met almost exclusively in the prepositional frame 'auf etwas hinauslaufen' — to amount to, to come down to, as in 'Das läuft auf dasselbe hinaus.' That is candidate_glosses index 1. The shipped literal sense is both the rarer one and slightly off in English besides, since laufen here is running rather than walking.

hindeuten.why: The shipped gloss took the physical-gesture sense, but the reading a learner meets is the evidential one in candidate_glosses index 2: 'alles deutet darauf hin, dass ...' — everything indicates/suggests that. Bare 'point' sends the learner to the gesture reading, for which German normally uses zeigen anyway.

hinfahren.why: The importer took the transitive haben-sense (driving someone else somewhere), which is comparatively rare. The reading a learner actually meets is the intransitive sein-sense in candidate_glosses index 1: to drive or travel there, as in 'Wie kommst du hin?' — 'Ich fahre hin.' Glossed as 'give a ride', a learner cannot parse that ordinary use at all.

hingeben.why: 'Hand over' names the plain physical transfer, which German expresses with übergeben, aushändigen or reichen; hingeben carries an elevated sense of relinquishing something valuable — 'sein Leben hingeben', and reflexively 'sich einer Sache hingeben'. Candidate_glosses index 1 has the right sense. Glossed as 'hand over', a learner would use it for passing the salt.

hingucken.why: The shipped gloss is a Wiktionary cross-reference, not a meaning: it points the learner at another German verb (hinsehen) instead of telling them what hingucken means. The verb is the colloquial (northern/central) equivalent of hinsehen: to direct one's gaze at something, to take a look.

hinrücken.why: The shortening dropped kaikki's '(from speaker)' and inverted the meaning in the process: English 'move away' reads as distancing oneself, i.e. wegrücken or abrücken. Hinrücken is shifting or scooting something toward a specified place — 'rück den Stuhl mal hin'. The hin- deixis is toward the target, not away from it.

hintanhalten.old: evite, try to make something not appear
hintanhalten.why: Not usable English. 'Evite' is an archaic Latinate rarity no learner (and few native speakers) will recognize, and the comma-joined remainder, 'try to make something not appear', is a dictionary paraphrase rather than a gloss. The verb is Austrian/administrative German for preventing or averting something before it can happen (Missbrauch hintanhalten).

hintanstellen.old: put back, order into a posterior position
hintanstellen.why: The leading synonym 'put back' reads as returning an object to its place, which is zurückstellen or zurücklegen, not this verb; and 'order into a posterior position' is stilted dictionary English. Hintanstellen means to place something last in priority, typically figuratively (seine eigenen Interessen hintanstellen = subordinate one's own interests).

hinwegsehen.why: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first, literal sense (looking over the top of something), while the sense a learner meets is the figurative one at candidate_glosses index 1: über etwas hinwegsehen = to disregard a fault, to turn a blind eye. The English 'look over' also misleads independently, since it usually means to examine.

hochdrehen.why: 'Turn upward' describes rotating something so it points up. The verb's everyday sense is increasing a setting by turning: die Heizung/die Musik hochdrehen, and den Motor hochdrehen for revving an engine. English 'turn up' carries exactly that and is what the learner needs.

hochfahren.why: 'Drive upwards/northwards' is kaikki's first-listed sense and the most marginal of the three; the reading a learner actually meets is candidate_glosses index 1, starting up a computer or system (den Rechner hochfahren, die Produktion hochfahren). The slashed 'upwards/northwards' also asks the learner to pick between two unrelated directions.

hochrechnen.old: calculate purposefully high in the dark
hochrechnen.why: The importer took kaikki's second, pejorative sense, and 'calculate purposefully high in the dark' is not usable English about anything. Hochrechnen is the neutral statistical verb behind Hochrechnung, the election-night projection: extrapolating a whole from a partial sample. Candidate_glosses index 0 has the right sense ('to project, to cast').

innehaben.why: Bare 'hold' presents this as a synonym of halten and invites the learner to write things like 'Ich habe das Buch inne'. Innehaben takes offices, posts, positions, and titles, never physical objects; the restriction is the whole of the word's meaning and candidate_glosses index 0 states it.

kehren.why: The comma presents two unrelated actions as synonyms: sweeping a floor and turning something around. kaikki lists only 'to sweep' (index 0), which is the living everyday sense (southern German's counterpart to fegen). The 'turn' reading survives mainly in fixed expressions (den Rücken kehren, in sich gekehrt) and should not be paired with 'sweep' as an equivalent.

klappen.why: 'work out, fold' joins two distinct senses with a comma, which the house style reads as 'these mean the same thing'. The sense a learner meets constantly is the impersonal 'das klappt' = it works out, it succeeds (candidate_glosses index 2); the hinge sense (index 1) is a separate meaning and mostly appears in prefixed forms such as umklappen, aufklappen, zuklappen.

kleinkriegen.why: Shortening to a bare 'break' drops the part that carried the meaning. kaikki's single sense is 'to break (psychologically)' (index 0), and the verb is overwhelmingly used of wearing a person down or of something indestructible (nicht kleinzukriegen sein). Unqualified 'break' points the learner at physical breakage, for which German uses kaputtmachen or zerbrechen.

kontrollieren.why: Leading with 'control' teaches the false friend. In ordinary German kontrollieren means to check or inspect (Fahrkarten kontrollieren, Ausweise kontrollieren), which is why kaikki lists 'to check' first (index 0); the 'exercise control over' reading is the narrower, largely business-register one. Pairing the two with a comma tells the learner the English words are interchangeable here, which is exactly the mistake that produces *ich kontrolliere meine Tickets = I control my tickets.

leichtfallen.why: The comma in 'come, be easy' is not a synonym separator but a split inside the phrase 'come easy'. Read by the app's house convention, where a comma means the items are equivalents, the gloss offers 'come' as a standalone meaning of leichtfallen, which is not a sense the verb has. The intended reading — 'das fällt mir leicht' = that comes easily to me, that is easy for me — survives only in the second half.

losgehen.why: 'leave' is the right direction but collides with verlassen and invites a transitive reading a learner will produce wrongly ('das Haus losgehen'). Losgehen is intransitive and means to set off or get going — 'wir gehen um acht los' — and the same word covers something getting under way, 'es geht gleich los' (candidate_glosses index 1). 'set off, get going' names that single sense without the verlassen collision.

losschlagen.why: The shipped 'knock loose' is the literal, technical sense (Putz losschlagen, loosening something by striking it), which a learner will almost never meet. In ordinary use losschlagen means to launch an attack or strike — 'die Armee schlug los', 'auf jemanden losschlagen' — which candidate_glosses lists at index 2 (and index 1). A secondary common sense is selling something off cheaply. The literal sense was taken because it is kaikki's first-listed, not because it is the encountered one.

mitbekommen.old: get or be given something when leaving
mitbekommen.why: The shipped sense (being given something to take with you, as in a dowry or a packed lunch) is real but marginal. The sense a learner meets constantly is candidate_glosses index 1: to catch, notice, or become aware of something — Hast du das mitbekommen?, Davon habe ich nichts mitbekommen. Shipping only the first-listed sense leaves the common one unglossed.

mitdenken.why: A bare 'follow' is too thin to identify the verb and collides with folgen, nachgehen, and mitkommen, all of which a learner will also meet. mitdenken means to think actively alongside a speaker or process — to keep up with the reasoning, or to use one's head rather than mechanically execute. kaikki offers nothing better, so the gloss needs writing rather than importing.

mitfahren.why: 'Drive with' is a Germanism that implies the subject is operating the vehicle, when mitfahren specifically means travelling as a passenger or accepting a ride: Kann ich mitfahren?, Sie ist bei ihm mitgefahren. The gloss points at the right situation but attributes the wrong role.

mitkriegen.why: Cross-reference rather than a meaning: 'synonym of mitbekommen' tells a learner nothing about the verb, and mitbekommen is itself mis-glossed in this corpus. Colloquial mitkriegen means to catch, notice, or pick up on something (Hast du das mitgekriegt?).

mitreißen.why: 'Entrain' is a fluid-dynamics term of art, and in ordinary English it means to board a train; either reading is useless or actively wrong for a learner. mitreißen means to sweep something along by force (der Fluss riss das Boot mit) and, figuratively, to carry an audience away. candidate_glosses index 1, 'to carry away', is the usable sense.

mitspielen.new: play along, join in a game
mitspielen.why: 'Cooperate' is the figurative extension (wenn das Wetter mitspielt), not the sense a learner meets. The everyday meaning is to take part in a game or play alongside others — candidate_glosses index 1, 'to play along'. Glossing it as 'cooperate' also collides with mitarbeiten and mitwirken, which ship that same word.

nachblicken.why: 'Look at' names a different action and would teach the learner to use nachblicken where German wants ansehen or anschauen. nachblicken is always jemandem nachblicken: to follow someone with one's eyes as they leave. The nach- component, which carries the whole meaning, is absent from the gloss.

nachempfinden.why: 'Feel for' reads as pity or sympathy, which is mitfühlen — and mitfühlen ships that exact phrase in this same corpus, so the two verbs are indistinguishable to a learner. nachempfinden is candidate_glosses index 0: to imaginatively re-experience how someone felt, hence to understand or relate to it (Das kann ich gut nachempfinden). The shipped gloss comes from index 1, the weaker sense.

nachsagen.old: repeat something said by someone else
nachsagen.why: The shipped sense (kaikki index 0, parroting what another person said) is the marginal one; that job is done in ordinary German by nachsprechen, which this shard glosses 'repeat'. The reading a learner actually meets is candidate index 1: jemandem etwas nachsagen, to say something (usually unflattering) about someone — 'man sagt ihm nach, er sei geizig', 'das kann man ihr nicht nachsagen'.

nachsetzen.why: 'Place after' is the technical typographic/grammatical sense (setting one element behind another) and is not what a learner encounters. The everyday reading is candidate index 1: jemandem nachsetzen, to give chase — 'die Polizei setzte dem Flüchtenden nach'. German Wiktionary lists the pursuit sense first.

niederschlagen.why: 'Defeat' is broadly in range but loose enough to mislead: it invites a learner to use niederschlagen where besiegen is wanted (a sports or election defeat), which German does not allow. The verb carries a forcible put-down — einen Aufstand, Proteste, Widerstand niederschlagen — which kaikki separates as index 1 'to quell (a rebellion)'.

niederstoßen.old: thrust down, knock down so that it falls)
niederstoßen.why: Mangled shortening: the gloss ends 'knock down so that it falls)' with an unbalanced closing parenthesis, because the shortener spliced the tail of kaikki's parenthetical clarification '(to hit or knock (something) so that it falls)' onto the definition. The verb simply means to thrust or knock something down.

offenhalten.why: The shipped gloss is a Wiktionary cross-reference, not English about the verb: it tells the learner to look up another German word. The meaning was in the same candidate entry (index 0, 'synonym of offenlassen; to keep open') but the shortening kept the pointer and discarded the definition. offenhalten means to keep something open — a door, a shop, a position, an option.

offenstehen.why: 'stay open' names duration, which belongs to offenbleiben. offenstehen is stative: 'Die Tür steht offen' is the door is open, not the door stays open. The imprecision was inherited from kaikki's own wording at index 0, so the gloss is broadly right but collides with a neighboring verb.

preisgeben.why: The shipped gloss takes kaikki's first sense (abandon/surrender), which in modern German is the literary one — 'dem Untergang preisgeben', 'sich preisgeben'. The sense a learner actually meets is candidate index 1: disclosing information, as in 'keine Details preisgeben', 'Daten preisgeben', 'seine Identität preisgeben', which is standard news and everyday German.

raushalten.new: stay out of, keep out of
raushalten.why: 'hold out' reads in English as endure or resist (German durchhalten), so it points at the wrong action. Even taken as physically holding something out — candidate index 1 — that is a marginal use of the clipped form. In practice raushalten is overwhelmingly reflexive: 'sich aus etwas raushalten', 'Halt dich da raus!', meaning to keep clear of a matter.

reinwaschen.why: The literal washing sense is marked rare in German dictionaries; in actual use reinwaschen is the figurative verb for clearing someone of suspicion or blame (sich von einem Verdacht reinwaschen, Geld reinwaschen). candidate_glosses lists that sense at index 1 ('to whitewash'). Shipping 'cleanse' also collides with reinigen, which is the verb a learner would actually reach for when they mean cleaning something.

richten.why: The comma reads as 'these mean the same thing', but 'direct' and 'judge' are unrelated senses of richten. 'Direct, aim, point' is the sense a learner meets constantly (etwas an jemanden richten, sich nach etwas richten, den Blick auf etwas richten); 'judge' is the elevated legal/biblical sense (ueber jemanden richten) behind the noun Richter and is rare in everyday German. Pairing them invites a learner to use richten for ordinary judging, where German wants beurteilen or urteilen. The correct sense is candidate index 0.

sattsehen.old: have enough of seeing something beautiful
sattsehen.why: Lifted verbatim from kaikki, and the English inverts the feeling. German sich an etwas sattsehen is satiation in the positive sense: to gaze at something as long as one wants, usually in the negative (ich kann mich nicht daran sattsehen, 'I can't get enough of looking at it'). English 'have enough of seeing something beautiful' reads idiomatically as being fed up with the sight, the opposite of what the verb conveys. It is also far longer than house style allows.

seligmachen.why: 'beatify' is the meaning of seligsprechen, which ships in this same corpus glossed exactly that way. seligmachen is to make blessed — to grant salvation or blessedness — not to perform the Church's act of declaring someone Blessed. The kaikki entry conflates the two neighbouring verbs, and the shipped gloss inherits the collision.

sorgen.why: The gloss leads with 'worry', which is the reflexive-only reading (sich sorgen) and is itself uncommon next to sich Sorgen machen. The verb a learner actually meets is 'für jemanden/etwas sorgen' — to take care of, to see to, to make sure something happens — which candidate_glosses lists at indices 0 and 1. Leading with the marginal sense, and pairing it by comma with the vague 'care', invites the reading that sorgen is primarily an emotion verb.

starkmachen.why: In real usage this verb is almost always reflexive — sich für jemanden/etwas starkmachen — meaning to campaign or stand up for a cause or person. That is candidate_glosses index 1 ('to support, advocate for'). The shipped 'strengthen' is kaikki's first-listed literal reading of stark + machen, and it also collides with stärken, which the corpus already glosses 'strengthen'. A learner will meet starkmachen in the advocacy sense.

teilhaben.why: teilhaben an etwas means to have a share in something, to partake of it — am Wohlstand teilhaben, am Erfolg teilhaben. The shipped 'participate' names the active taking-part sense that belongs to teilnehmen, which this same corpus glosses identically as 'participate'. Two distinct verbs ending up with the same gloss erases the distinction between having a share in something and taking part in it.

thematisieren.why: 'make topic' is not an English phrase — it is a shortening of something like 'make a topic of' that lost the article and the preposition, leaving a fragment the learner cannot use. The first half, 'address', is correct; candidate_glosses index 0 ('to bring up, address an issue') gives the sense cleanly.

umschlagen.why: A bare 'turn' reads as rotation and collides with drehen and wenden. The core sense of umschlagen is an abrupt switch into an opposite state, said of weather, mood, or a situation: 'Das Wetter schlug um', 'Die Stimmung schlug in Wut um'. The gloss points at the right action but so loosely that it names nothing distinctive.

umsteigen.why: The shortening dropped the part of candidate_glosses index 0 that carried the meaning, '(from one means of transport to another)', leaving three vague synonyms. 'interchange' is the misleading one: as an English verb it means to swap two things for each other, which umsteigen never means. The verb is what you do when you get off one train or bus and onto another.

umstimmen.why: The shipped 'retune' is the technical musical sense (ein Instrument umstimmen), which a learner will essentially never meet. In ordinary German umstimmen means to change someone's mind, to talk someone round: 'Ich konnte ihn doch noch umstimmen.' That sense is candidate_glosses index 1.

umtreiben.why: 'drive around' is the archaic agricultural sense (driving livestock about). In modern German umtreiben is used almost exclusively for something that occupies or troubles a person's thoughts: 'Diese Frage treibt mich seit Wochen um', 'Was treibt dich um?' That is candidate_glosses index 1, listed there as 'to worry (someone)'.

umwenden.why: The comma presents 'turn over' and 'turn inside out' as synonyms, but they are different actions, and the second is not really umwenden's territory anyway: turning a garment inside out is umkrempeln or umstülpen. umwenden is turning something onto its other side, as with a page or a pancake. The stray half came in with candidate_glosses index 0.

unterfangen.why: The living verb is reflexive: sich unterfangen = to dare, to presume, to have the audacity ("Wie kannst du dich unterfangen, so zu reden?"). That is candidate_glosses index 1. The shipped "undertake" belongs to the noun das Unterfangen (an undertaking); as a verb it is archaic, and the only other current verbal use is the construction term for underpinning a foundation. A learner shown "undertake" will reach for unterfangen where unternehmen is wanted.

untergehen.why: The bare one-word "set" is a fragment of candidate_glosses index 0, where the parenthetical ("of a heavenly body: to disappear below the horizon") carried all the meaning. Stripped of it, "set" reads as place, put, or harden, none of which this verb does. The verb's core is going down or under, spanning the sun setting, a ship sinking, and an empire perishing; a gloss naming that motion covers all of them.

unterhalten.why: The comma presents two distinct senses as synonyms: entertaining a guest (candidate index 1) and maintaining a building or a fleet (index 0). House style reads a comma as "these mean the same thing," so this teaches that "entertain" and "maintain" are interchangeable renderings. Entertain is the right sense to keep, being the one a learner meets first alongside the reflexive sich unterhalten.

verabschieden.why: Two unrelated senses joined by a comma: sich verabschieden = say goodbye (candidate index 0) and ein Gesetz verabschieden = pass a law (index 4). Read as house-style synonyms, "say goodbye, pass" invites the reading "pass away," which the verb does not mean. Ship the everyday sense alone.

verbiegen.why: "something" is kaikki's transitivity placeholder, retained from candidate index 0 ("to bend something."), where it existed only to distinguish that entry from index 1's intransitive "to bend, become bent." It is dictionary scaffolding rather than part of the meaning, and no other gloss in the corpus carries a dummy object.

verbuchen.why: 'post' is the technical accounting sense (post an entry to a ledger), but as a bare one-word gloss it reads to a learner as posting a letter or posting online, neither of which verbuchen means. The verb is to book or record an entry, and by extension to chalk something up ('einen Erfolg verbuchen'). candidate_glosses index 2 ('to register, book') is the unambiguous wording.

verfehlen.why: 'meet or hit not' is broken English carried over verbatim from kaikki — a word-for-word calque of German 'nicht treffen' with the negation stranded at the end. The leading 'miss' already carries the meaning correctly (das Ziel verfehlen, seinen Zweck verfehlen); the trailing fragment is apparatus, not a synonym, and should be dropped.

vergelten.why: vergelten is neutral as to whether what is repaid is good or bad — 'Vergelt's Gott' (may God reward you) and 'Böses mit Bösem vergelten' are the same verb. 'retaliate' narrows it to revenge only, and is intransitive in English where vergelten is transitive, so it also mismodels the syntax. candidate_glosses carries both halves separately (index 0 'retaliate', index 1 'reward'); a single neutral gloss covers both.

verhaften.why: verhaften means to arrest — the everyday police sense, which candidate_glosses lists at index 1 ('to imprison, to put into confinement after judicial writ'). The shipped gloss lifts kaikki's sense 0, a philosophical/literary paraphrase ('stop moving and instead stick'), which is both the wrong sense and unusable as English: a learner reading it would never connect it to 'Die Polizei hat ihn verhaftet.'

verheiraten.why: 'marry (someone)' is the gloss for heiraten, not verheiraten. heiraten is what the spouses do ('Sie heiratet ihn'); verheiraten is what a third party does — give in marriage, marry off ('Er verheiratete seine Tochter'), or officiate. candidate_glosses index 1 has it: 'to marry off; to find a spouse for'. As shipped, the gloss teaches the learner to use verheiraten where heiraten is required, a classic error.

verhelfen.why: Bare 'help' is the gloss for helfen and loses everything the ver- prefix adds. verhelfen is always jemandem zu etwas verhelfen — to help someone get or achieve something ('Das verhalf ihm zum Sieg'). kaikki's index 0 kept the preposition as 'to help (to)'; the shortening dropped it, leaving a gloss that collides with a different, more basic verb.

verkehren.why: 'interact in someone’s sphere' is leaked dictionary paraphrase, not English about the verb — it names no action a learner could recognize or produce. The senses actually met are: of transport, to run or operate on a route ('Die Linie verkehrt stündlich'), which is the everyday one; also 'mit jemandem verkehren' (associate with) and 'ins Gegenteil verkehren' (turn into its opposite). The transport sense is inside kaikki's index 0, buried after the paraphrase as 'to operate'.

verkriechen.why: "creep away" is a literal reading of ver- plus kriechen that keeps the manner and drops the point: sich verkriechen is about ending up hidden — sich ins Bett / unter die Decke verkriechen, said of a person who withdraws from the world. Candidate index 1 ("to hide away, to be holed up") names the sense in use; as shipped the gloss collides with wegschleichen.

verlauten.why: Verlauten is reportive and subjectless in normal use — wie aus Regierungskreisen verlautet, es verlautete, dass… — so the meaning runs in the opposite direction from "announce", which is what the causative verlauten lassen adds. The shipped gloss teaches the wrong argument structure for the bare verb.

verleben.why: Bare "spend" is ambiguous in English and, next to a German verb, reads first as spending money — which is ausgeben. Verleben takes only time as its object: den Sommer bei den Großeltern verleben.

verlernen.why: The importer took kaikki's second sense (index 1). "cease doing" names a different action — that is aufhören. Verlernen means to lose a skill through lack of practice: Ich habe mein Französisch verlernt. Sense index 0 has it right: lose the ability to do a task due to rarely doing it. Because the house comma reads as "these mean the same thing", the shipped gloss presents stopping and forgetting-how as equivalents.

verloben.why: Leaked dictionary apparatus: the trailing "‘someone’])" is the tail of kaikki's argument-structure note "(optional [with mit (+ dative) ‘someone’])", cut mid-bracket. As shipped it is not English about the verb. Sich verloben means to become engaged to be married.

verlöschen.why: Verlöschen as a learner meets it is intransitive: die Kerze verlischt, das Feuer verlosch — the flame or light dies out on its own. The transitive "extinguish" is löschen (or auslöschen); glossing the ver- verb as "quench, extinguish" invites the learner to produce *ich verlösche das Feuer. The intransitive reading is candidate index 1.

verrechnen.why: The shortening kept the definitional first half of candidate index 0 and dropped the half that named the action: "particularly: to offset one against another". "calculate several quantities together" is a description of an entry rather than a usable English rendering — a learner cannot substitute it into a sentence for etwas mit etwas verrechnen.

verschlagen.why: The shortening kept an unfiltered synonym pile from candidate index 0 and dropped the parenthetical that made it interpretable. 'shlep' is a Yiddish-derived regionalism opaque to a German learner reading English, and 'bring' floating at the end of the list is so general it names nothing. The verb's live use is the near-impersonal 'es hat ihn nach München verschlagen' — chance carried him somewhere he did not intend to go — so 'strand' plus a directional 'drive' carries it; 'shlep' and 'bring' should go.

versehen.why: The gloss welds two unrelated senses into one comma list, which the house style reads as synonyms: 'equip' renders transitive 'etwas mit etwas versehen' (candidate index 3, 'to provide with'), while 'make mistake' renders the reflexive 'sich versehen' (candidate index 4), a separate and much rarer reading. A learner sees 'equip' and 'make mistake' presented as equivalents. The second half is also ungrammatical English, missing its article. The sense to ship is the transitive one: to furnish or provide something with something.

verstoßen.why: 'violate, expel' pairs two genuinely different constructions as if they were synonyms: 'gegen etwas verstoßen' means to violate or infringe a rule (candidate index 1), while 'jemanden verstoßen' means to cast out or disown (candidate index 0). The first is far more frequent and is the one a learner meets, in news German especially. Committing to it removes the false equivalence.

vertreiben.why: The comma joins two unrelated senses, which the house style reads as synonyms: 'drive out' is candidate sense 0 (jemanden vertreiben) and 'distribute' is the commercial sense 2 (to market or sell in quantity). A learner reading them as equivalents may take vertreiben for verteilen. Ship the expulsion sense, which is the one a learner meets first and the one the app's related verbs (austreiben, verjagen) sit beside.

verweben.why: kaikki offers only the bare 'to weave', which is weben, not verweben. The ver- prefix carries the sense of weaving things together: verweben is to interweave or interlace, and its commonest modern use is the figurative participle (eng miteinander verwoben). Glossed as 'weave' the verb collides with weben and invites a learner to write 'einen Teppich verweben'.

verweisen.why: Same comma collision: 'refer' is candidate sense 0 (auf etwas verweisen) and 'expel' is candidate sense 2 (jemanden von der Schule verweisen), and the house style presents them as synonyms. Referring is much the commoner reading and the one that governs the verb's usual prepositional frame.

vonstattengehen.why: 'take place' is stattfinden, and the shipped gloss makes the two look interchangeable. vonstattengehen is almost always used with a manner adverbial — reibungslos, zügig, langsam vonstattengehen — and means how a process runs, which is candidate sense 1 ('to proceed'). A learner given 'take place' will write 'Das Konzert geht vonstatten', which is not German.

vorbilden.why: The verb means to give someone preliminary training or education — 'gut vorgebildet' is the everyday use, and the adjective 'vorgebildet' means qualified or trained. 'Preform' is a technical/literal reading (shaping material in advance) that a learner will not meet, and in English it is also easily misread as a typo for 'perform'. candidate_glosses index 1 ('to prelearn; to prepare; to equip with knowledge in advance') is the sense the app should ship.

vorbringen.why: The shortening dropped the qualifier that carried the meaning: kaikki's sense is 'to say (in the sense of to allege or state something)'. Bare 'say' makes vorbringen indistinguishable from sagen, when the verb specifically means to advance or raise something — an argument, an objection, a complaint (Einwände vorbringen, Beschwerde vorbringen). The action is right but the rendering is too vague to be usable.

vorhalten.why: The sense a learner actually meets is 'jemandem etwas vorhalten' — to hold something against someone, to reproach them with it — which is candidate_glosses index 1 and the dominant use in modern journalistic German. The shipped 'hold up' names the literal index-0 sense, and as bare English it invites the far commoner readings 'delay' and 'rob', neither of which the German verb carries.

vorlesen.why: The shortening dropped the parenthetical that did all the work: kaikki reads 'to read (aloud)'. Bare 'read' collides with the base verb lesen and loses the vor- component entirely — vorlesen is specifically reading aloud to someone (dem Kind eine Geschichte vorlesen), never silent reading.

vorsetzen.why: 'Prefix' is a narrow grammatical/technical sense that kaikki happens to list first; a learner reading it will think of morphology or computing. The ordinary meaning is to place something in front of someone, above all to set food or drink before them (man setzte uns eine Suppe vor). candidate_glosses index 1 ('to serve (food or drink)') and index 2 ('to put in front; to move forward') are the senses in real use.

vorsingen.why: The shortening stripped '(something to someone)', leaving a gloss identical in force to the base verb singen. vorsingen is singing for an audience of one or more listeners — and by extension auditioning (candidate_glosses index 1).
