Bare 'sing' teaches nothing that distinguishes the prefixed verb.

vorwerfen.why: The importer took kaikki's first-listed literal sense. Physically throwing something forward is now largely confined to the fixed image of throwing someone to the lions; the sense a learner meets constantly is 'jemandem etwas vorwerfen' — to accuse someone of something, to reproach them — which is candidate_glosses index 2. As shipped, the gloss teaches the wrong action for one of the most frequent verbs in German news prose.

vorziehen.why: 'Pull to the front' is kaikki's first-listed literal sense, but the everyday use is 'to prefer' — es vorziehen, etwas zu tun; ich ziehe Tee vor. That is candidate_glosses index 2. The literal sense is comparatively rare, so a learner is taught a reading they will seldom encounter and denied the one they will.

wegdrängen.why: 'edge away' is intransitive in English — it describes the subject retreating slowly — whereas wegdrängen is transitive and forceful: jemanden wegdrängen is to shove someone aside, and figuratively to crowd out or force out (a competitor, a thought). The gloss reverses the agency and loses drängen (push, press) entirely; 'edge off' is not idiomatic English at all. The defect is inherited verbatim from candidate 0, which is the only candidate.

wegführen.why: wegführen is führen (lead), not tragen (carry): 'Die Polizei führte den Mann weg' means the police led the man away, and 'der Weg führt vom Dorf weg' means the path leads away from the village. The gloss inherits kaikki's mistranslation (candidate 0, the only candidate) and collides exactly with wegtragen, which is glossed 'carry away' in this same shard — so the two verbs currently ship indistinguishable glosses and the one on wegführen is the wrong action.

wehren.why: In modern German wehren is essentially reflexive — sich wehren, to defend oneself or fight back (candidate 0 says exactly this). Bare 'defend' reads transitively and points the learner at verteidigen, inviting wrong German like 'ich wehre meine Heimat'. 'resist' is on target; 'defend' needs the reflexive to be accurate.

weismachen.why: The shortening dropped kaikki's '[with dative]' label (candidate 0), and what survives is the English fixed phrase 'make believe', which means to pretend or play imaginatively. jemandem etwas weismachen means the opposite kind of act: to deceive someone into believing something untrue ('Das kannst du mir nicht weismachen'). The learner is left with the English idiom rather than the German verb's meaning.

weiterarbeiten.why: 'resume' asserts an interruption that weiter- does not: weiterarbeiten is to keep working, to carry on working ('Arbeite weiter!' means keep at it, not start again). The rest of the weiter- cluster in this shard is glossed consistently as continuation — weiterfahren 'continue driving', weiterlesen 'continue reading', weiterleben 'live on' — so this one is the outlier, and it shifts the aspect.

weiterkämpfen.old: continue to battle after a pause
weiterkämpfen.why: 'continue to battle' is right, but the trailing 'after a pause' is a false restriction imported from the dictionary definition: weiterkämpfen is simply to fight on, with or without an interruption ('trotz der Verletzung weiterkämpfen'). It also runs far past the app's house length for a sense this simple.

widersetzen.old: set against, make a stand against
widersetzen.why: sich widersetzen + dative means to oppose, defy, or resist. Bare 'set against' is not idiomatic English for that: it reads as 'place in opposition to' or 'offset', and only works as opposition in the reflexive 'set oneself against'. The natural gloss is already present as candidate index 1 ('to defy, to oppose, to resist'). The shipped gloss points at the right action but names it in English a learner cannot reuse.

wiedergeben.why: 'reproduce, return' joins two unrelated actions with a comma, which the house style reads as 'these mean the same thing'. Worse, the weaker half leads the learner astray: modern German returns objects with zurückgeben, and wiedergeben in the give-back sense (candidate index 0) is formal and dated. The live senses are rendering or restating content (candidate index 1) and playing back audio or video (candidate index 2), both of which 'reproduce, render' covers.

wundern.why: Leading with 'wonder' teaches a false friend. German wundern is transitive 'to surprise, astonish' (es wundert mich, dass...) and reflexive sich wundern 'to be surprised, be amazed' (candidate index 0 and 1). It does not carry English 'wonder' in its ordinary modern sense of asking oneself something — that is sich fragen — so a learner given this gloss will produce *ich wundere mich, ob... for 'I wonder whether'. Candidate index 2's 'to wonder' is Wiktionary rendering the archaic 'wonder at' construction, which a learner will not read that way.

zerwerfen.why: 'Break by throwing' is the regional literal sense; in ordinary modern German zerwerfen appears reflexively, 'sich mit jemandem zerwerfen', meaning to quarrel and break off relations. That sense is candidate index 1. The shipped gloss also duplicates zerschmeißen exactly, which is the verb that does carry the throwing sense.

zeugen.why: The comma presents two unrelated senses as synonyms: begetting a child and bearing witness. The house style reads a comma as 'these mean the same thing', so a learner sees one blurred meaning rather than either real one. The core transitive verb is 'ein Kind zeugen' (candidate index 0). The witness sense is nearly always intransitive with a preposition ('das zeugt von Mut'), and 'testify' additionally misleads because courtroom testimony in German is aussagen. Ship the transitive sense.

zubringen.why: The everyday meaning of zubringen is spending time somewhere ('er brachte den Tag im Bett zu'), which candidate_glosses lists at index 1. The shipped 'bring' is the regional literal sense of herbeibringen, which survives mainly in the noun Zubringer, and as a gloss it is indistinguishable from plain bringen.

zufliegen.why: The shortening dropped the '(toward)' that candidate index 0 carried, leaving a gloss identical to plain fliegen. The directional zu- is the whole content of the verb, so the learner is given nothing that distinguishes it.

zugreifen.why: The gloss leads with the computing sense (candidate index 2) and joins it by comma to the physical sense, so two different senses are presented as synonyms. The sense a learner meets is grabbing or seizing quickly (candidate index 0), and by extension helping oneself at the table. 'Access' should not head the gloss.

zuhalten.why: "be keep something shut" is not English — the importer copied a malformed Wiktionary line (candidate_glosses index 0 reads "to be keep something shut") verbatim, so the defect survived the shortening step. The verb means to hold something shut: die Tür zuhalten, sich die Nase zuhalten, sich die Ohren zuhalten.

zukehren.why: "turn something" drops the directional zu- that is the entire content of the verb, and kaikki's index 0 ("to turn (rotate) something") actively pushes toward the wrong reading: zukehren is not rotating, it is turning a side of something toward a person or place. Its dominant use is jemandem den Rücken / das Gesicht zukehren.

zuleiten.why: The shortening dropped the parenthetical that carried the meaning: kaikki index 0 is "to feed (a liquid, electricity, etc.)", and bare "feed" reads as füttern, a verb zuleiten never means. Zuleiten is to channel or supply something along a conduit — Wasser, Strom, Frischluft zuleiten — and by extension to forward a document to an office.

zunähen.why: "suture" is a surgical term, but zunähen is the ordinary domestic word for sewing something closed — ein Loch, eine Naht, eine Tasche zunähen. The register mismatch will keep a learner from using the verb where it actually belongs. candidate_glosses index 1 ("to stitch up") is the everyday equivalent.

zurichten.why: "hurt" is a weak Wiktionary gloss the importer took at face value. Zurichten is not the German for hurting someone — that is verletzen or wehtun — and in current usage it appears almost exclusively as übel/schlimm zurichten, meaning to batter someone or leave something in a wrecked state. Glossed as "hurt", it invites a learner to write ich habe ihn zugerichtet for "I hurt him", which is badly wrong.

zurufen.why: Bare "call" collides head-on with anrufen, the verb for telephoning, which is the reading a learner will reach for first. Zurufen is to call out to someone across a distance: er rief mir eine Warnung zu.

zurückstehen.why: The shipped gloss takes the literal spatial reading, but in use zurückstehen is overwhelmingly figurative: hinter jemandem zurückstehen (be inferior to, rank below) and zurückstehen müssen (go without so others can go first). candidate_glosses lists these at index 1 and index 2. The English 'stand behind' is additionally treacherous, since it reads as 'support' to an English speaker — the opposite of the German.

zusammenbringen.why: Bare 'collect' names sammeln, not zusammenbringen. The sense a learner meets is bringing people or things together — zwei Menschen zusammenbringen, Familien zusammenbringen — which candidate_glosses lists at index 3. The importer took kaikki's first-listed sense, which here is a marginal reading.

zusammendrängen.why: 'Condense' is the figurative, text-editing sense; the primary sense is physical, especially reflexive — die Menschen drängten sich zusammen, to crowd or press into a small space. candidate_glosses has it at index 1. Duden orders it the same way, with the condensing sense marked as transferred use.

zusammenfahren.why: The sense a learner actually meets is the startle reaction — er fuhr zusammen, als es klingelte — which candidate_glosses lists at index 1. For vehicle collisions German normally uses zusammenstoßen, so glossing this verb as 'collide' both ships the rarer sense and points the learner at the wrong word for the common one.

zusammennehmen.why: 'Add up, total' corresponds only to the fixed adverbial alles zusammengenommen (all things considered), not to the live verb. In use zusammennehmen means gathering one's resources — allen Mut zusammennehmen, seine Kräfte zusammennehmen — and reflexively sich zusammennehmen, to get a grip on oneself. candidate_glosses has the mustering sense at index 2 and the composure sense at index 3.

zuschlagen.why: 'Take one's chance' is a real colloquial sense (bei einem Angebot zuschlagen), but the sense a learner meets first and most is physical: to strike or hit — der Täter schlug mehrfach zu. That is candidate_glosses index 0, whose kaikki wording ('avail oneself of one's muscular power and direct it to a striking face') is unusable as-is and presumably why the importer skipped past it to index 1.

zutreiben.why: In isolation English 'drive' reads as operating a vehicle, which is fahren and exactly wrong here. Zutreiben is to drive something — cattle, a herd, a boat — toward a destination, or intransitively to drift toward one ('das Boot trieb dem Ufer zu'). Candidate index 0 carries the directional complement that the shortening stripped, leaving a gloss that points at the wrong action.

zuwenden.why: Bare 'turn' is what wenden or drehen mean and loses the directional component that is the whole content of the zu- prefix. Zuwenden is to orient toward something or someone, usually reflexive — 'sie wandte sich ihm zu', 'sich einem Thema zuwenden'. As shipped, the gloss reads as rotating an object, which the verb does not describe. Candidate index 2 has the right sense.

überarbeiten.why: The comma presents two different senses as synonyms. Transitive überarbeiten means to revise or rework a text or a design (candidate index 0); 'overwork' is the reflexive sich überarbeiten (candidate index 1), a distinct construction. A learner reading the comma as equivalence would write *'ich überarbeite' for 'I am overworking', dropping the obligatory reflexive pronoun. The gloss should commit to the transitive sense, which is the one the learner meets first.

überblicken.why: Neither word works. In current English 'oversee' means to supervise, which is beaufsichtigen, not überblicken; and 'overview' is a noun, not a verb, so the second item is unusable as English. Überblicken means to take in the whole of something at a glance, literally ('vom Turm die ganze Stadt überblicken') or figuratively ('die Lage überblicken', to grasp the situation). The correct sense is absent from candidate_glosses, which reproduces the same two bad items.

überführen.why: The synonym list was imported unfiltered and 'translate' came with it. That item reflects the narrow ecclesiastical sense of translating relics or a bishop's see, not anything a learner will use, and it sits next to the German verb übersetzen, which really does mean translate — so the gloss actively invites a false equivalence. The other three items correctly render the transport sense at candidate index 0.

übergehen.why: The comma joins senses belonging to two different verbs. Inseparable übergehen (übergeht, überging, hat übergangen) means to pass someone over, skip, or ignore — 'er wurde bei der Beförderung übergangen'. 'Go over to' is the separable ÜBERgehen (geht über, ist übergegangen), as in 'zum nächsten Punkt übergehen' or 'in Rauch übergehen', a different action with a different conjugation. Since the entry ships as inseparable, the gloss must commit to the skip sense, which candidate_glosses gives at indices 0 and 1.

überhören.why: 'Mishear' is the wrong English word and collides with sich verhören, which is the verb for hearing something incorrectly. Überhören means not to register an utterance at all — either accidentally ('das habe ich überhört', I missed that) or deliberately ('eine Bemerkung überhören', to let a remark pass). The shortening from candidate index 0 dropped the '(deliberately)' that made the source phrasing barely defensible, leaving a wrong equivalence behind.

überkommen.why: 'Conquer' names a different verb. Überkommen does not describe defeating or surmounting something — that is überwinden, besiegen, or erobern. In überkommen the emotion is the subject and the person the object: 'mich überkam ein Gefühl der Angst', a feeling came over me. The shipped gloss reverses the argument structure and would produce wrong German such as *'ich überkam meine Angst'. Candidate index 1 ('to overwhelm') is closer, but 'come over' is what the verb actually does.

überlassen.why: 'Abandon' names a different action and is presented as a synonym of the correct one. Überlassen is to let someone else have something or to leave a matter up to them — 'ich überlasse dir das Auto', 'das überlasse ich dir'. Abandoning something is verlassen or aufgeben; the reading only surfaces in the fixed phrase 'jemanden seinem Schicksal überlassen', which is too narrow to carry the gloss. Both candidate glosses describe the relinquish-to-someone sense only.

überschauen.why: English 'overlook' is dominantly read as 'fail to notice', which is what übersehen means — and übersehen ships with exactly that gloss elsewhere in the corpus, so the two collide and the learner is taught the opposite of überschauen. überschauen is to take in the whole of something at a glance: to survey it and comprehend its extent (candidate_glosses index 1 has 'to grasp, to assess, to comprehend'). kaikki's index 0 'to overlook' is the archaic 'look out over' reading, not the modern one.

überschlagen.why: Skipping a page or passage is a real but secondary reading. Duden leads the transitive entry with 'flüchtig, ungefähr berechnen', and Kosten/den Preis überschlagen is the use a learner actually meets; kaikki's ordering here is entry order, not frequency. The right sense is candidate_glosses index 1.

überschreiben.why: Signing property over is the narrowest and rarest of this verb's readings — legal register, seldom encountered. The senses a learner meets are the computing one (candidate_glosses indices 2 and 3, 'to overwrite') and giving a text a heading (index 1). Shipping the conveyancing sense sends a learner looking for a notary when the word they will actually see is about a file being replaced.

überspielen.why: 'sth' is a dictionary abbreviation for 'something' that survived the import; it is apparatus, not English, and leaves the gloss reading as an unfinished phrase. The sense itself — copying or dubbing a recording onto another medium — is right and just needs the placeholder removed.

überstimmen.why: überstimmen is specifically defeating someone by majority vote — the stem is Stimme, 'vote'. English 'overrule' names an authority setting a decision aside (German aufheben, verwerfen), which does not require a vote at all and could send a learner to the wrong word in a courtroom or committee context. candidate_glosses index 1 has the precise equivalent.
